headline: Approved Eversource conduit on Newton Street, a Home Rule Petition on anticoagulant rodenticides, and three ordinances; referred a $2,082,498 fire truck bond.
summary: Members approved a Newton Street utility conduit project, a body armor grant, an Armory arts space lease, and several grants and fund transfers. Many traffic, parking, and public health requests were sent to committees for discussion.
decisions: Approved a citation commending Gonzalo Puigbo for his work as Executive Director of Somerville Community Corporation.
Approved the remembrances.
Approved the minutes of the Special Meeting of July 27, 2026.
Approved the Eversource Grant of Location to install 140 feet of conduit in Newton Street.

Approved and sent to the Traffic and Parking Committee for discussion an order asking the Director of Parking to discuss the feasibility of considering vehicle size and weight when setting residential parking permit fees.
Approved and sent to the Public Health and Public Safety Committee for discussion an order asking for an update on dumpster license registration and enforcement.
Approved a resolution asking the Administration to develop a procedure for towing vehicles parked in locations such as fire lanes that pose a public safety concern.

Approved and sent to the Finance Committee for discussion an order asking the Director of Finance and the Director of Economic Development to report on the financial bankruptcy involving investor funds holding equity in the empty lab building at 808 Windsor Place, Boynton Yards.
Approved a resolution in remembrance of Lobga Rangzen and in recognition of Somerville’s Tibetan Community.
Placed on file the resignation of Councilor Mbah from the City Council.
Approved and sent to the Traffic and Parking Committee for discussion a resolution asking for drop-off and pick-up signage on Cherry Street, across from the Kennedy School.
Approved and sent to the Traffic and Parking Committee for discussion a resolution asking for bike racks at the Kennedy School.
Approved and sent to the Traffic and Parking Committee for discussion a resolution asking for bike markings in the bike lane on Elm Street, across from the Kennedy School.
Approved and sent to the Traffic and Parking Committee for discussion a resolution asking for a NO TURN ON RED sign at Broadway and Cedar Street.
Approved and sent for discussion a resolution asking the Director of Mobility to make the intersection of Vernon Street and Partridge Avenue safer.
Approved and sent to the Finance Committee for discussion a resolution asking for a memo on the cost of staffing Somerville High School as a teen center after school hours.
Approved and sent to the Traffic and Parking Committee for discussion a resolution asking the Director of Mobility to discuss strategies for safety concerns caused by large trucks on Weston Avenue.

Approved and sent to the Traffic and Parking Committee for discussion a resolution asking the Director of Parking to issue free temporary parking permits for residents whose driveways are obstructed by city construction.
Approved a resolution in support of the "Yes in God’s Backyard" (YIGBY) legislation.
Approved a resolution in support of an act relative to preventing home insurers from forcing tree removal.
Approved the Finance Committee report of September 22, 2026.
Approved accepting and spending a $9,809.81 grant requiring a match from the U.S. Bureau of Justice Assistance for Police Department body armor vests.
Approved appropriating $255,045 from the Transportation Network Receipts Reserved Account for Fiscal Year 2027 Vision Zero efforts.
Approved accepting and spending a $215,919.15 grant with no new match from the Metropolitan Area Planning Council for the Health and Human Services Department.
Approved accepting and spending a $24,500 grant with no new match from the State 911 Department for emergency medical dispatch.
Approved accepting and spending a $295,463 grant with no new match from the State 911 Department for E911 dispatcher personnel costs.
Approved accepting and spending a $159,754.04 grant with no new match from the State 911 Department for E911 dispatcher training costs.
Approved appropriating $350,000 from the Immigrant Legal Services Stabilization Fund for legal services for immigrants and asylum seekers. Vote was 10-0, with Ward Two Councilor Scott absent.
Approved paying prior year invoices totaling $80,852.95 from Department of Public Works accounts.
Approved lease agreements with various tenants for commercial arts space at the Somerville Armory Building, 191 Highland Avenue. Vote was 10-0, with Ward Two Councilor Scott absent.
Approved the Legislative Matters Committee report of September 8, 2026.
Approved the Legislative Matters Committee report of September 15, 2026.
Ordained an amendment to Section 2-323 of the Code of Ordinances to update categories and salaries for non-union positions. Vote was 10-0, with Ward Two Councilor Scott absent.
Ordained an amendment to Chapter 3, Article VIII, Division 1 of the Code of Ordinances. Vote was 10-0, with Ward Two Councilor Scott absent.
Approved the Davis Square Neighborhood Council comments on formal recognition as a neighborhood council. Vote was 10-0, with Ward Two Councilor Scott absent.
Recorded the Davis Square Neighborhood Council information on its recognition request as work completed.
Approved a Home Rule Petition to regulate anticoagulant rodenticides. Vote was 10-0, with Ward Two Councilor Scott absent.
Recorded the comments of 6 residents on Davis Square Neighborhood Council recognition as work completed.
Ordained an amendment to Chapter 6 of the Code of Ordinances. Vote was 10-0, with Ward Two Councilor Scott absent.
Approved the Licenses and Permits Committee report of September 23, 2026.
Approved a new Extended Operating Hours License for Wings Over Somerville, 519 Somerville Avenue, until 2am.
Referred to the Legislative Matters Committee for recommendation an amendment to Chapter 15, Article III of the Code of Ordinances.
Referred to the Finance Committee for recommendation a request to borrow $2,082,498 in a bond for an Aerial Ladder Truck and a Rescue Truck for the Fire Department.
Approved appropriating $19,986 from the Salary Contingency Account to fund a collective bargaining agreement with Local 888 - Crossing Guards.
Referred to the Finance Committee for recommendation a transfer of $153,987 from the CPA Community Housing Debt Service account to the CPA Community Housing Reserve.
Referred to the Finance Committee for recommendation a transfer of $22,596.24 from the CPA Historic Preservation Debt Service account to the CPA Historic Preservation Reserve.
Approved establishing a Grant Match Account with a $15,000 transfer for the Massachusetts Department of Agriculture's Fiscal Year 2027 Food Security Infrastructure Grant match.
Referred to the Finance Committee for recommendation a time-only contract extension until 2/15/2027 for Utile Inc.
Referred to the Finance Committee for recommendation payment of prior year invoices totaling $10,224.39 for legal services.
Approved paying a prior year invoice totaling $2,500 for manager training.
Approved paying prior year invoices totaling $2,000 for pre-employment drug testing and physicals.
Approved paying a prior year invoice totaling $1,912.50 for a 111F record review.
Referred to the Finance Committee for recommendation a $297,679 grant from the Mass Department of Mental Health for the Metro Boston Crisis Intervention Training and Technical Assistance Center.
Referred to the Finance Committee for recommendation a $169,000 grant from Urban Areas Security Initiative for school security equipment.
Approved accepting and spending a $59,497 grant requiring a match for expanding cold storage capacity of the Somerville Mobile Farmers Market.
Referred to the Finance Committee for recommendation a $57,925 grant from the Mass Department of Mental Health for the jail/arrest diversion program.
Referred to the Confirmation of Appointments and Personnel Matters Committee for recommendation the appointment of Ashley Tienken to the Affordable Housing Trust.
Placed on file and sent to the Legislative Matters Committee for discussion an update on the Civilian Oversight policy development process.
Approved a request by the City Clerk to hold a special election to fill vacancies in the Ward 2 and Ward 3 City Council seats.
Placed on file and sent to the Housing, Community Development and Equity Committee for discussion the 2025 Office of Housing Stability Annual Report.
Placed on file the City Clerk's report of Block Party Licenses issued.
Approved renewing the taxi medallion license for Raymy Inc, Med #59.
Approved renewing the taxi medallion license for SSR Cab Inc, Med. #81.
Approved a Public Event License for the Davis Square Neighborhood Yard Sale on September 27.
Approved a Public Event License for the Italian Heritage Month Flag Raising on October 15.
Placed on file comments and a petition from 89 registered voters requesting a public hearing on Police Body-Worn Cameras.
Placed on file comments from 9 residents on Davis Square Neighborhood Council recognition.
Placed on file comments and a petition from 74 registered voters requesting a public hearing on the proposed ethical procurement ordinance.
Placed on file comments from Stephanie Lee of Verizon on the Verizon Copper Network Retirement.

Referred to the School Building Facilities and Maintenance Committee for recommendation an order asking the Director of Infrastructure and Asset Management to present on concerns with exterior tiles on the Somerville High School building.
Approved a Public Event License for The Autumn 5k Fun Run on September 26.
Approved a Public Event License for the Harvest Festival on October 3.
Approved a Public Event License for the Gurk McGurk Back to School Corps and Cars Show on October 4.
Placed on file comments from the Pedestrian and Transit Advisory Committee on Squires Bridge.
Placed on file comments from Adrienne Naylor on bike lanes on McGrath.
Placed on file comments from Frank Privitera on Magoun Square.
Placed on file comments from 4 residents on the Warming Center.

# City of Somerville, Massachusetts · City Council · Meeting Minutes

Thursday, September 24, 2026 · 7:00 PM

NOTICE: This is NOT the official version of the City Council's minutes. While reasonable efforts have · been made to assure the accuracy of the data provided, do not rely on this information without first · checking with the City Clerk.

## 1. OPENING CEREMONIES

The meeting was called to order at 7:03 PM by Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis. The City Council entered recess at 8:17 PM and returned at 8:28 PM.

1.1. Roll Call

Call of the Roll.

## (ID # 26-1438 ) RESULT: PLACED ON FILE

- Present: Ward Three City Councilor Ben Ewen-Campen
- City Councilor At Large Jon Link
- Ward Four City Councilor Jesse Clingan
- City Councilor At Large Kristen Strezo
- Ward Five City Councilor Naima Sait
- City Councilor At Large Ben Wheeler
- Ward Seven City Councilor Emily Hardt
- Ward One City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin
- City Councilor At Large Wilfred N. Mbah
- Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis

## Absent:

Ward Two City Councilor Jefferson Thomas (J.T.) Scott

1.2. Remembrances Remembrances.

## (ID # 26-1439 ) RESULT: APPROVED

1.3. Minutes

Approval of the Minutes of the Special Meeting of July 27, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1440 ) RESULT: APPROVED

## 2. CITATIONS

2.1. Citation

By Councilor Strezo

(ID # 26-1410 ) Commending Gonzalo Puigbo for his work as the Executive Director of Somerville Community Corporation.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## 3. PUBLIC HEARINGS

3.1. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 140 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1400 ) Newton Street, from the intersection of Prospect Street and Newton Street to a point of pickup at existing Manhole 31233.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## 4. ORDERS, ORDINANCES, RESOLUTIONS AND MOTIONS OF MEMBERS

4.1. Order

By Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1420 ) That the Director of Parking discuss with this Council the feasibility of considering vehicle size and weight when establishing residential parking

permit fees, so that permit costs may better reflect the amount of parking space used and the relative impact of different sized vehicles on city streets.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Traffic and Parking Committee

4.2. Order

By Councilor Wheeler, Councilor Hardt and Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1421 ) That, in view of the proliferation of rats in the city, the Director of Public

- Health and/or designees update this Council on the status of dumpster

license registration and enforcement, including: estimates of the numbers of licensed and unlicensed dumpsters in the city which regularly contain

discarded food; procedures for identifying unlicensed dumpsters and encouraging licensing; criteria for approval of dumpsters; staff capacity for dumpster inspection and enforcement; and current methods and best

- practices for excluding rodents from dumpsters.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Public Health and Public Safety Committee

4.3. Resolution

By Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1419 ) That the Administration develop a procedure allowing the Parking

- Department, upon identifying a vehicle parked in a location such as a fire

lane where it poses a public safety concern, to arrange for the vehicle to be towed.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.4. Order

By Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-1429 ) That the Director of Finance and the Director of Economic Development

report to this Council on the situation of financial bankruptcy, involving the investor funds, holding equity in the empty lab building at 808 Windsor

- Place, Boynton Yards.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Finance Committee

4.5. Resolution

By Councilor Mbah, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor Clingan, (ID # 26-1428 ) Councilor Davis, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Link, Councilor McLaughlin, Councilor Sait, Councilor Strezo and Councilor Wheeler

- In remembrance of Lobga Rangzen and in recognition of Somerville’s
- Tibetan Community.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.6. Communication By Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-1395 ) Conveying his resignation from the City Council.

## RESULT: PLACED ON FILE

4.7. Resolution

By Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1422 ) That the Director of the Parking install drop-off/pick-up signage on Cherry

Street, across from the Kennedy School.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Traffic and Parking Committee

4.8. Resolution

By Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1423 ) That the Director of Mobility add bike racks at the Kennedy School.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Traffic and Parking Committee

4.9. Resolution

By Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1424 ) That the Director of Mobility paint bike markings in the bike lane on Elm

Street, across from the Kennedy school.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Traffic and Parking Committee

4.10. Resolution

By Councilor Sait and Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1425 ) That the Director of Mobility install a NO TURN ON RED sign at the intersection of Broadway and Cedar Street.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Traffic and Parking Committee

4.11. Resolution

By Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1426 ) That the Director of Mobility take the steps necessary to make the intersection of Vernon Street and Partridge Avenue safer.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Traffic and Parking Committee

4.12. Resolution

By Councilor Sait and Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1427 ) That the Administration and relevant departments submit a memo to this

Council showing the cost of staffing Somerville High School to be used as a teen center after school hours.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Finance Committee

4.13. Resolution

By Councilor Hardt, Councilor Strezo and Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1430 ) That the Director of Mobility discuss with this Council possible strategies to address safety concerns caused by large trucks using Weston Avenue as a

cut-through from Broadway to Clarendon Avenue, particularly the dangerous conditions created when these trucks make a right turn from

- Weston Avenue onto Clarendon Avenue.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Traffic and Parking Committee

4.14. Resolution

By Councilor Link and Councilor Ewen-Campen

(ID # 26-1431 ) That the Director of Parking issue free temporary parking permits for

- residents who do not have a parking permit and whose driveways are
- temporarily obstructed by ongoing city construction projects.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Traffic and Parking Committee

4.15. Resolution

By Councilor Link, Councilor Mbah, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor

(ID # 26-1432 ) Strezo, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Sait and Councilor Wheeler

In support of the "Yes in God’s Backyard" (YIGBY) legislation.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.16. Resolution

By Councilor Link, Councilor Sait, Councilor Scott and Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1433 ) In support of an act relative to preventing home insurers from forcing tree

removal.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## 5. UNFINISHED BUSINESS

## 6. REPORTS OF COMMITTEES

- 6.A. FINANCE COMMITTEE
- 6.A.1. Committee Report Report of the Committee on Finance, meeting on September 22, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1435 ) RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.2. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $9,809.81 grant that requires a

(ID # 26-1221 ) match, from the United States Bureau of Justice Assistance to the Somerville Police Department for body armor vests.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.3. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to appropriate $255,045 from the Transportation

(ID # 26-1240 ) Network Receipts Reserved Account to the Transportation Network

Revolving Account for Fiscal Year 2027 Vision Zero efforts.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.4. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $215,919.15 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1254 ) match required, from the Metropolitan Area Planning Council to the Health

- and Human Services Department for a Shared Services Coordinator and a
- Clinical Community Health Worker.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.5. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $24,500 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1320 ) match required, from the State 911 Department to the Police Department for

emergency medical dispatch.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.6. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $295,463 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1322 ) match required, from the State 911 Department to the Police Department for

E911 dispatcher personnel costs.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.7. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $159,754.04 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1323 ) match required, from the State 911 Department to the Police Department for

training costs for E911 dispatcher certification and recertification.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.8. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to appropriate $350,000 from the Immigrant Legal

(ID # 26-1334 ) Services Stabilization Fund for legal services for immigrants and asylum

seekers seeking permanent residency.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## AYE:

- Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen, City Councilor
- At Large Link, Ward Four City Councilor Clingan, City
- Councilor At Large Strezo, Ward Five City Councilor Sait,
- City Councilor At Large Wheeler, Ward Seven City
- Councilor Hardt, Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin,
- City Councilor At Large Mbah, and Ward Six City
- Councilor Davis
- ABSENT: Ward Two City Councilor Scott

6.A.9. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to pay prior year invoices totaling $80,852.95 using

(ID # 26-1341 ) available funds in various Department of Public Works accounts for various

services.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.10.Mayor's Request Requesting approval to enter into lease agreements with various tenants to (ID # 26-1354 ) provide commercial arts space at the Somerville Armory Building, 191

Highland Avenue.

## RESULT: APPROVED AYE:

- Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen, City Councilor
- At Large Link, Ward Four City Councilor Clingan, City
- Councilor At Large Strezo, Ward Five City Councilor Sait,
- City Councilor At Large Wheeler, Ward Seven City
- Councilor Hardt, Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin,
- City Councilor At Large Mbah, and Ward Six City
- Councilor Davis
- ABSENT: Ward Two City Councilor Scott

6.B. LEGISLATIVE MATTERS COMMITTEE

6.B.1. Committee Report Report of the Committee on Legislative Matters, meeting on September 8, (ID # 26-1441 ) 2026.
